newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on Cetes demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on Cetes demand.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained early modest gains from the dollar at the close of trade on Tuesday in the wake of sustained demand for money market instruments despite forecast falls in primary rates, traders said.
"The market has already discounted the expected fall in primary interest rates," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 0.3 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8690/7.8710 and 7.8650/7.8680 per dollar.

Money market traders surveyed by Reuters forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 21.22 percent at the primary auction due later in the day. This would entail a fall of 139 basis points since last week's auction.
"There were no buyers (of dollars); that's why the peso firmed up despite predictions interest rates will fall," another trader said.
Dealers said lower yields on U.S. long bonds meant that Cetes rates would still be attractive to foreign investors, even after forecast cuts in auction rates.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 19/32 to yield 7.04 percent in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.05 centavos firmer at 7.8610/7.8635 per dollar.
